title: November 23 — Pisara and VirtualTuft: time as memory, measured against strong controls
summary: Two sister experiments grew from coffee drips, Shaw's faucet, Takens embeddings and delayed recurrent neurons. Pisara separates periodic readout-free echoes/omission timing from decorrelated temporal embeddings; VirtualTuft isolates leaky/nonlinear memory from explicit feedback, correcting weak linear baselines and odd-symmetric tanh bias. Strong controls often outperform or tie the loops. Neither shows biological tuft computation or general law discovery.

nodes.claim: One-node continuous-time pulse simulator tests coincidence-tuned feedback delay for rhythmic echo/omission timing and decorrelation-tuned delays for Takens-style histories with k-NN, linear or quadratic readouts.
nodes.survived: Under a favorable 600 ms period-two lock, the echo signals omitted drops around 4–5 ms from their expected time; Gate 6 explicit lag-two phase clock ties the loop's median performance. Seven delayed trace coordinates with fixed quadratic readout score about 0.017–0.018 Hénon NMSE, versus 0.008–0.009 with a k-NN archive.
nodes.killed: An earlier crippled quadratic baseline and jitter-trigger artifact were corrected. The learned delay has harmonic basins, ratchets on draining inputs, and Gate 4 fusion fails to improve forecasting. Some omission scores use windows centered on actual withheld events and are not yet fully prospective alarms; no biological apical computation is shown.
nodes.era: November 23: physical timing and virtual time-memory

nodes.claim: Single time-multiplexed tanh node with 50 virtual slots compares delayed feedback, ordinary leaky state, stateless cascades, local gain adaptation and matched explicit nonlinear-history predictors on synthetic drop and hidden-state worlds.
nodes.survived: After a fixed, label-independent bias corrected odd-symmetry, explicit returning feedback improved over the leaky-only reservoir on noisy Hénon (0.0732→0.0630 MAE) and a delayed quadratic world (0.0991→0.0753 MAE), across five held-out seeds.
nodes.killed: Centered quadratic history still wins (0.0370 and 0.0314 MAE), and the simple adaptive gain rule fails. Gate 0's apparent nonlinear advantage over linear taps disappeared with stronger polynomial controls; 50 virtual slots are not a physically mapped cortex or a native homogeneous 2D Luotain2 field.

edges.why: Two experiments created from the same coffee-drip/Takens/apical-loop question: Pisara emphasizes continuous-time coincidence and omission; VirtualTuft emphasizes virtual-node representation and delayed-feedback ablations. They are independent implementations, not a code fork.
Both use delayed observations as dynamical coordinates, but Pisara asks how temporal traces become predictive rather than visualizing sound phase spaces.
Luotain2 provides an outside-observer identification question; VirtualTuft explicitly treats its node×time trace as not yet suitable for Luotain2's spatial FFT grammar, deferring a validated audit.

motifs.title: Time as physical memory: recurrence helps some states, but strong explicit history often wins
motifs.description: Pisara shows coincidence-tuned echoes and distinct decorrelation-based temporal representations while acknowledging that a simple phase-preserving clock can tie its omission timing. VirtualTuft shows a biased returning-feedback contribution on two hidden-state surrogates but nonlinear historical features still win. There is no evidence here that either synthetic system models dendritic tufts in living neurons.
